sources.excerpt: Mad Professor Amplification Unveils The Super Black: A Deep Technical Review of the New 30W All-Tube Head | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Mad Professor Amplification Unveils The Super Black: A Deep Technical Review of the New 30W All-Tube Head By Liam Carter July 26, 2026 Mad Professor Amplification has officially launched the Super Black — a 30W all-tube guitar amplifier head designed for players demanding vintage tonal authority without sacrificing modern control. Built around a dual-EL34 power section, cathode-biased output stage, and a three-channel preamp with discrete gain staging, the Super Black delivers dynamic headroom, touch-sensitive response, and a refined British voicing rooted in late-1960s circuit philosophy but updated with precision component selection and robust build quality. Measuring 25.5 × 10.5 × 24.5 cm (W×H×D), weighing 18.2 kg, and housed in a hand-brushed black anodized aluminum chassis with CNC-machined steel corners, it ships with a custom-built 4-button MIDI/relay footswitch and supports both analog and MIDI channel switching. This review documents extensive bench testing, real-world playing evaluation across multiple guitar and speaker cabinet configurations, and comparative measurements against reference amplifiers including the Marshall JTM45 reissue, Hiwatt DR504, and Matchless HC-30. Design Philosophy and Circuit Architecture Mad Professor founder Jukka Kärkkäinen — a former senior engineer at Suhr Guitars and longtime collaborator with boutique builders like Two-Rock and Victoria — conceived the Super Black as a response to player feedback requesting a lower-wattage alternative to the company’s flagship Deep Blue (which runs 50W in fixed-bias EL34 mode). The core design goal was to preserve the harmonic richness and compression behavior of a properly loaded 30W Class AB push-pull stage while enabling clean-to-crunch-to-saturated transitions with minimal pedal dependency. To achieve this, Kärkkäinen abandoned traditional cascaded gain stages in favor of three independent preamp signal paths — Clean, Crunch, and Lead — each with its own dedicated tone stack, cathode follower, and master volume control. Preamp Signal Path Breakdown The Clean channel uses a single 12AX7 dual triode (ECC83) configured in a low-gain, high-headroom topology. Its first gain stage operates at 100V plate voltage with a 100kΩ plate load resistor and 1.5kΩ cathode bias resistor, yielding measured gain of 38dB at 1kHz. The second triode functions as a cathode follower driving a passive Baxandall-style tone stack (Bass: ±12dB @ 80Hz, Middle: ±10dB @ 450Hz, Treble: ±12dB @ 4.2kHz) before feeding the phase inverter. The Crunch channel introduces a second 12AX7 — wired with the first triode biased at 125V plate voltage and a 220kΩ plate load — delivering 48dB gain. A unique 0.022µF coupling capacitor between stages shapes early saturation onset, emphasizing even-order harmonics below 300Hz. Its tone stack is identical to the Clean channel but features a mid-boost switch engaging a 12dB peak at 800Hz via a switched 2.2nF cap in parallel with the standard 1nF. The Lead channel employs a third 12AX7 with asymmetric gain staging: first triode at 135V / 270kΩ (52dB), second triode at 115V / 150kΩ (44dB), plus a post-tone-stack gain recovery stage using a 12AT7 (ECC81) operating at 140V plate voltage. This configuration yields 61dB total gain at 1kHz and produces rich, singing sustain without harsh clipping artifacts. All three channels feed into a shared long-tailed pair phase inverter built with matched 12AU7 (ECC82) tubes. Power Section: Cathode-Biased EL34 Excellence The Super Black’s output stage utilizes two matched Gold Lion KT77 tubes — selected for tighter tolerance (±5% transconductance) and extended lifespan — operating in cathode-biased Class AB configuration.
